_about: Naturalization rules the N-400 calculator applies (src/naturalization.py). Copied from the Form N-400 Instructions, edition 01/20/25 (uscis.gov/n-400, saved 2026-10-01 to data/reference/n-400instr.pdf), page numbers below. Re-check when USCIS publishes a new N-400 edition (docs/maintenance.md, item form_n400).

General._: LPR 5 years; physical presence 30 months (913 days) in the past 5 years (Instructions p. 3, p. 19)

Spouse of U.S. citizen._: LPR 3 years, married to and living in marital union with a U.S. citizen for 3 years, spouse a citizen for 3 years; 18 months (548 days) in the past 3 years (Instructions p. 4, p. 19)

_early_filing: May file up to 90 days before reaching the 5- or 3-year continuous residence period, but must meet every other requirement at filing (Instructions, Early Filing).
_state_residence: Lived in the state or USCIS district for at least 3 months before filing (Instructions p. 3, '3-Month Residency').
_absence: An absence of more than 6 months but less than 1 year must be explained (the client shows residence wasn't broken); an absence of 1 year or more breaks continuous residence unless an N-470 was approved (Instructions, Continuous Residence, pp. 17-18). When the client may file again after a break is the attorney's call.

english_exemptions.text: 50/20: no English test; civics in the client's language
55/15: no English test; civics in the client's language

_english_exemptions: Age and years as a permanent resident at the time of filing (Instructions, Naturalization Testing and Exceptions).
_fee_reduction: Reduced fee when household income is at or below 400% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines for the household size (Instructions, Part 10); evidence: each household member's most recent federal tax return, or pay stubs / W-2 / SSA-1099.

selective_service._: Men who lived in the U.S. (except as a lawful nonimmigrant) between 18 and 26 must have registered; if not, a status information letter and an explanation (Instructions, Part 9 items 22.a-22.c).
